source_row.rationale: ACOG notes that postpartum baby blues commonly begin a few days after delivery and usually improve within days to one or two weeks without treatment. Option B fits the timing, mild symptoms, and spontaneous resolution. Option A and D describe depression despite a short, self-limited course. Option C is inconsistent with the absence of severe psychotic symptoms and the benign resolution.
source_row.source_detail: ACOG Postpartum Depression FAQ — Baby Blues: onset about 2–3 days postpartum and usually improve within a few days to 1–2 weeks without treatment. ACOG FAQ published 2024-04, last reviewed 2025-12; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity; coping, support systems, grief/loss and therapeutic adaptation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A postpartum client had tearfulness and mood swings beginning a few days after birth that resolved without treatment within two weeks. Which interpretation is most accurate?
